answer: Time-locked reputation release: each new identity’s reputation accrues only after a fixed delay, and transfers out are capped per period. Clones earn nothing until the horizon passes. An attacker must fund every clone’s hosting and delay costs across that full horizon, and any early exit forfeits accrued value, so each additional clone is negative-EV. The tide of new identities also raises the shared resource cost, while legitimate users keep their garden of reputation intact.
